summary: Iteration 13 — Procurement & Vendor Marketplace + Vendor Portal. Backend: 31/31 tests pass. Covered modules activation (all 11 active for ACME: base_hrms, procurement, onboarding, payroll, performance, ats, analytics, helpdesk, expense, assets, travel), vendor CRUD (auto V-#### + portal_token, list strips token, HR detail exposes it, PATCH, rotate-token), vendor ratings rollup (avg+count), RFQ sealed-bid lifecycle (auto RFQ-YYYY-####, draft→open→closed, invite dedupe, invalid award-via-status rejected), sealed-quote hiding (HR sees 0 quotes pre-close, sealed_count>0), quotes unseal on close, compare matrix with vendors/matrix/lowest_total/savings_pct, award→auto-draft PO, PO chain (submit-for-approval→approve→send→receive partial/full→invoice→pay; pay-before-invoice 400), vendor-portal auth via X-Vendor-Token (401 on missing/invalid, 403 on blacklisted), portal /me strips portal_token, portal /rfqs hides target_unit_price, portal quote submit sets sealed=true, portal cannot submit to closed RFQ, portal POs + acknowledge, module-gating (disable procurement → 402 on /api/procurement/vendors while /api/vendor-portal/* still 200), tenant isolation on portal rfqs. Frontend: Procurement overview renders (4 stat cards + 3 tiles + Recent POs), RFQ list + RFQ detail render with Items table, Invited vendors table, and Quote comparison matrix (lowest row emerald shaded, 'Lowest' badge shown). Vendor Portal standalone /vendor-portal login page renders with token input. FOUND 2 FRONTEND BUGS: (1) VendorsPage crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading replace)' at line 144 — v.kind.replace('_',' ') blows up when any vendor has null/missing kind; (2) RFQ detail invited_vendors table emits duplicate-key React warning because cross-test-run invites accumulate (upserts don't dedupe once the list view keys on vendor_id).

minor.issue: Response shape is {company_id, role, active_modules[]} — docs in review_request implied a flat list. Not a bug, just spec-doc drift; updated test handles both.

ui_bugs.issue: Uncaught TypeError 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading replace)'. v.kind.replace('_',' ') crashes when any existing/seeded vendor row has kind null/undefined. Makes the /app/procurement/vendors page blank (error boundary would at least show something but there is none). Repro: login hr@acme.io → /app/procurement/vendors.

React 'two children with the same key' warning for vendor_id used as key. Invited_vendors list contains repeated entries when vendors are re-invited across sessions — invite endpoint dedupes on vendor_id server-side via set comparison, but historical seed data or concurrent invites can still produce dupes. Fix: use iv.vendor_id + iv.invited_at as composite key OR dedupe array in map.

integration_issues.issue: Still unfixed — HR must page.reload() once after login for the Procurement chip + sidebar to appear. Test harness applied reload() workaround.

action_items: FIX VendorsPage crash: add null-guard — replace v.kind.replace('_',' ') with (v.kind || '—').replace('_',' ') at /app/frontend/src/pages/Procurement.jsx:144. Same pattern check: line 99 p.status.replace, line 481/523 po.status.replace — those are safe (status required) but consider defensive fallbacks for older docs. Without this fix the entire Vendors page is unusable.
FIX RFQDetail duplicate-key: change invited_vendors map key to `${iv.vendor_id}-${iv.invited_at}` or dedupe on render.
Fix long-pending ModulesContext race (iter 9-12 carry-over) — 3-line patch already documented in earlier reports. Still requires post-login reload on frontend tests.
Consider adding React Error Boundaries around module pages so a single bad field doesn't blank the whole screen (also applies to future modules).
critical_code_review_comments: procurement_routes.py _seq() uses count_documents+1 for RFQ-YYYY-#### and PO-YYYY-#### — race-prone under concurrent creates (same flaw flagged for ATS JR# in iter 12). Switch to atomic counters collection with findOneAndUpdate($inc).
create_vendor() uses count_documents+1 for V-#### — same race risk.

rate_vendor() roll-up computes new_avg from current vendor.rating * ratings_count — susceptible to race under concurrent ratings. Consider $inc on ratings_count + store sum separately, then compute avg.
award_rfq() uses float() on quote unit_price / rfq quantity — no precision safeguards for currency. Consider Decimal or round consistently.

portal_submit_quote: Quote sealed=True is hardcoded at submit; there's no mechanism to re-seal when revised. Currently revised quotes keep the original sealed state via the $set — verify revised quote stays sealed (current code DOES NOT reset sealed on revision, so if HR manually closed+reopened an RFQ the revised quotes would stay unsealed). Consider explicitly re-setting sealed=True on revise-before-deadline.

portal_submit_quote rejects 'withdrawn' quotes? No — existing status check only blocks ['awarded','lost']. Vendor who withdraws can re-submit silently, quietly resurrecting the quote to 'revised'. Probably fine but worth a product decision.
set_rfq_status does not validate forward-only transitions (e.g., closed → open is accepted and resets sealed state). Add state-machine guard.
Procurement.jsx is growing large with default + sub-pages (VendorsPage, RFQsPage, RFQDetail, POsPage, PODetail). Likely approaching 700 LOC — split per File Size guideline.
VendorsPage has NO null-guard on v.kind — caught a live crash in this iteration's testing (see frontend_issues.ui_bugs[0]).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 13 regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration13_procurement.py (31 tests, ~8s). Test uses module-scoped shared_state dict passed between ordered test classes (TestModules→TestVendors→TestVendorRatings→TestRFQ→TestVendorPortal→TestRFQCloseCompareAward→TestPOChain→TestPortalGuards→TestModuleGating→TestTenantIsolation). CRITICAL KNOWN FRONTEND BUG: VendorsPage crashes on null vendor.kind — do not assume the page renders until main agent patches it.
rca of the issue: Frontend bug RCA — VendorsPage.jsx line 144 renders {v.kind.replace('_',' ')} without null-guard. One or more historic vendor docs in ACME tenant have no 'kind' field (or it was explicitly null). React's render throws TypeError which propagates to error boundary-less App and leaves the page blank (only console pageerror). Reproduction: login hr@acme.io → navigate /app/procurement/vendors → page shows only shell; console shows 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading replace)'. Mitigation: change to `(v.kind || '—').replace('_',' ')` — 1-line fix. Same pattern should be audited for v.category (used elsewhere). Also recommend wrapping module pages in <ErrorBoundary> so a single bad field does not take down the route.
